# Ezra Chapter 7 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 470r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EZR_007_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Some time later, during the reign of King Artaxerxes of Persia, a man named Ezra made the journey from Babylon. He was the son of Seraiah, son of Azariah, son of Hilkiah, **2** son of Shallum, son of Zadok, son of Ahitub, **3** son of Amariah, son of Azariah, son of Meraioth, **4** son of Zerahiah, son of Uzzi, son of Bukki, **5** son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the chief priest.

**6** This Ezra came from Babylon. He was an expert in the Law of Moses, which the LORD, the God of Israel, had given. The king gave him everything he asked for, because the LORD his God was helping him.

**7** A number of Israelites came to Jerusalem with him in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes, including priests, Levites, musicians, gatekeepers, and temple servants.

**8** Ezra arrived in Jerusalem in the fifth month of the seventh year of the king's reign. **9** He had left Babylon on the first day of the first month and arrived in Jerusalem on the first day of the fifth month — a four-month journey — because God's gracious hand was on him.

**10** Ezra had devoted himself to studying the LORD's Law, to living by it, and to teaching its decrees and regulations throughout Israel.

**11** Here is a copy of the letter that King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra the priest and scholar, an expert in the LORD's commands and statutes for Israel:

**12** "From Artaxerxes, king of kings. To Ezra the priest, an expert in the Law of the God of heaven. Greetings.

**13** I hereby decree that any of the Israelites in my kingdom, including their priests and Levites, who wish to go to Jerusalem, may go with you. **14** You are being sent by the king and his seven advisors to evaluate conditions in Judah and Jerusalem according to the Law of your God, which you carry with you. **15** You are also to bring the silver and gold that the king and his advisors have voluntarily contributed to the God of Israel, whose dwelling is in Jerusalem, **16** together with all the silver and gold you may collect throughout the province of Babylon, including freewill offerings from the people and priests for the temple of their God in Jerusalem.

**17** Use this money to purchase bulls, rams, and lambs, along with the required grain offerings and drink offerings, and sacrifice them on the altar of your God's temple in Jerusalem.

**18** You and your fellow Jews may use the remaining silver and gold for whatever seems best, in accordance with the will of your God. **19** Deliver to the God of Jerusalem the articles entrusted to you for use in the temple. **20** If you need anything else for your God's temple, you may draw on the royal treasury.

**21** I, King Artaxerxes, order all treasurers in the province west of the Euphrates: Whatever Ezra the priest, the expert in the Law of the God of heaven, requests of you, provide it in full — **22** up to 100 talents of silver, 100 cors of wheat, 100 baths of wine, 100 baths of oil, and unlimited salt.

**23** Be careful to provide whatever the God of heaven demands for his temple, so that his wrath does not fall on the king and his sons. **24** Also be aware that you may not impose taxes, tribute, or duties on any of the priests, Levites, musicians, gatekeepers, temple servants, or other workers at this temple.

**25** And you, Ezra, using the God-given wisdom you possess, are to appoint magistrates and judges to administer justice for all the people in the province west of the Euphrates — everyone who knows the laws of your God. You must also teach those who do not know them. **26** Anyone who refuses to obey the law of your God or the law of the king will be punished strictly — by death, banishment, confiscation of property, or imprisonment."

**27** Praise the LORD, the God of our ancestors, who put it in the king's heart to bring honor to the LORD's temple in Jerusalem! **28** The LORD showed me his faithful love by giving me favor with the king, his advisors, and all his powerful officials. Because the LORD my God was with me, I took courage and gathered leaders from Israel to return with me.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 10 — The ideal scholar:** This single verse has shaped Jewish intellectual life for millennia. Ezra's three commitments — study, practice, teaching — established the pattern for every rabbi who followed. Notice the order: understanding comes before action, and action before teaching. A teacher who does not practice what he teaches has no authority; a practitioner who does not study has no foundation.

**Verses 12-26 — An empire serving God's purposes:** The lavishness of Artaxerxes' support is almost bewildering. A pagan emperor funds Jewish worship, exempts the clergy from taxation, and empowers a Jewish priest to enforce Torah law with the full backing of imperial authority. The author sees no contradiction — this is how God works in history, using empires as instruments of his will, even when those empires do not know him.

**Verse 27-28 — First-person breakthrough:** After six chapters of third-person narrative, Ezra's own voice suddenly breaks through. His first words are not about politics or logistics but praise: "Blessed be the LORD." The shift from bureaucratic Aramaic to personal Hebrew doxology mirrors the movement from imperial decree to heartfelt worship.

*— PNEUMA*
